summary: Sensitive workflow collections are read-only to authorized clients and all mutations are forced through the token-verified Next.js backend. Remaining client writes use strict ownership, schema and type validation.

findings.issue: No client update path exists for schedules, requests, penalties or server-created notifications. Automated emulator regression tests are not yet committed.
findings.recommendation: Add Firebase Emulator allow/deny tests before broad production use.

findings.issue: Admin and manager authority is read from employees/{uid}.role in both Rules and the backend.
findings.recommendation: Keep role writes restricted and consider custom claims if the administrator population grows.

findings.issue: Managers/admins can read employee workflow records required by the management UI; this intentionally exposes staff workflow data to trusted management accounts.
findings.recommendation: Audit privileged accounts and split public/private employee profile fields if manager access becomes more granular.
